question.leadin: The Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa paved the way for successful later sieges of Cordoba and Seville in this conflict.
question.text: Name this religious conflict between Christian states and Muslim states in the Iberian Peninsula, which is named for the reacquisition of traditionally Christian lands.
question.clue: The end of this period was marked by the signing of the Alhambra Decree.

swap.leadin: Pope Sixtus V supported this fleet that was defeated with the help of the "Protestant Wind"
swap.text: Name this royal navy sent by Philip II in 1588 to invade England and restore Catholicism.
swap.answerHtml: Spanish Armada [or la Grande y Felicísma Armada, or the Great and Most Fortunate Navy]
swap.clue: The plan was for this force to join with one under Alessandro Farnese, but before that could happen, it participated in its first engagement off Eddystone.

question.text: Merged with the Carlists by Franco, this Spanish fascist movement was founded by Jose Antonio Primo de Rivera.
question.clue: Two leaders of this party were buried within the Santa Cruz Basilica at the Valley of the Fallen.

swap.text: The Duke of Wellington also led troops during the Peninsular War, a war over control of this location. This region contains Spain and Portugal, and is separated from France by the Pyrenees.
swap.clue: The knight El Cid fought on both sides of a series of military campaigns in this region, which concluded in 1492 with the fall of the Emirate of Granada.

question.leadin: This treaty replaced the papal bull Inter caetera, which was issued by Alexander VI.
question.text: Identify this 1494 treaty that gave all lands west of an imaginary line in the New World to Spain and all lands east of it to Portugal. It was rendered moot when Portugal claimed lands west of the line anyway.
question.clue: This treaty established a line 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands, which was later extended through both poles by the Treaty of Zaragoza.

swap.leadin: This war was supposed to be avoided through the First and Second Partition Treaties.
swap.text: Name this 13-year conflict over control of an Iberian nation. It was sparked by the death of the childless King Charles II.
swap.clue: This conflict, which includes the battles of Malplaquet and Blenheim, was noted for the military success of Prince Eugene of Savoy and was fought in North America as *Queen Anne's War.

question.leadin: This man gained nationwide prestige after he crushed the Asturias miners' strike of 1934.
question.text: Name this man, who sent the Blue Division to fight for Nazi Germany on the Eastern Front during World War II. This dictator ruled his country under the title El Caudillo and came to prominence for his services in the Rif War.
question.clue: He was able to gain the support of the Carlists in forming the Falange party, and allowed the Blue Division to fight against the USSR during World War II.

swap.text: ETA ("etuh") seeks independence for this region of Spain. This region's namesake language is an isolate that has a pidgin with Icelandic due to meetings between whalers from this region and Icelandic fishermen.
swap.clue: The GAL, an illegal paramilitary group founded by the government of F´elipe Gonzalez, once operated in this region to fight the ETA, a terrorist group that promoted this region's separation.

question.text: In 1835, the Foreign Legion was employed by Maria Cristina, the consort of Ferdinand VIII, to put down a rebellion of this faction. This group was an offshoot of the clerical-friendly apostolico faction and opposed the Constitution of 1812.
question.clue: They had earlier supported the count of Montemolin, the son of their first leader, and refused to capitulate despite the setbacks faced by two of their key commanders, Maroto and Cabrera.

swap.text: The Reconquista officially ended with the capture of this city, the capital of the Nasrid Kingdom, in 1492. This city's last ruler, Boabdil, was forced to surrender it and the Alhambra Palace to Ferdinand and Isabel.
swap.clue: Following his honeymoon with Isabella of Portugal, Charles V had a palace constructed by Diego Machuca within the walls of this city's most famous structure.

question.text: This daughter of Ferdinand and Isabella and wife of Phillip the Handsome was a Queen of Spain who suffered from mental illness and was forced to live in a nunnery for much of her reign.
question.answerHtml: Joanna the Mad [or Juana la Loca; or Joanna of Castile; or Juana de Castilla]
question.clue: After the death of her husband, Philip the Handsome, this mother of Charles V and Ferdinand I spent the last fifty years of her life mourning her husband, usually locked in a castle at Tordesillas.

swap.text: Before the founding of the UAW, automotive workers got into a battle named after this city during a strike against Electric Auto-Lite. A war named after this city resulted from a dispute about the southern border of Michigan.
swap.clue: In the twelfth and thirteenth century, under the patronage of Alfonso the Wise, this city became a centre of translation of Arabic works.

question.text: The Alhambra Decree, which expelled the Jews from Spain, was advocated by this Dominican Grand Inquisitor under Ferdinand and Isabella.
question.clue: The co-rulers were also ardent supporters of the Inquisition, appointing this "hammer of heretics" as the brutal Grand Inquisitor.

swap.leadin: Ringtones featuring this person's voice became popular after he interrupted Hugo Chavez, asking him, "Why don't you shut up?"
swap.text: Name this ruler of Spain from 1975 to 2014, when he abdicated in favor of his son Felipe VI. This ruler oversaw the Spanish transition to democracy.
swap.clue: This head of state asked Hugo Chavez "Why don't you shut up?" at a meeting where Chavez repeatedly interrupted one of his countrymen.

question.text: The formation of a coalition government with the far-right CEDA party during the Second Republic era led socialists and anarchists to organize a 1934 general strike in this province of Spain, during which miners marched and captured the capital.
question.clue: This kingdom ended when its ruler moved out of its last capital at Oviedo in the Cantabrian Mountains.

swap.text: This first name was held both by a "Great" king of Pamplona and his three grandsons, who name a 1060s conflict in which Castile reconquered Alava. A later king with this name was the father of Berengaria of Navarre, who married Richard I of England.
swap.clue: This name of several kings of Navarre and Castille. Another king with this name turned a 1212 battle with an uphill charge that forced Muhammad al-Nasir to retreat.

question.leadin: The grocer Manuela Beltran helped trigger this revolt by tearing down tax hike notices, and it was part of a wave of unrest in South American colonies in the 1770s and 1780s with Tupac Amaru II's revolt.
question.text: Name this colonial tax revolt led by Beltran and Jose Antonio Galan against the Viceroyalty of New Granada. It shares its name with a revolt of Castilian city councils in support of Joanna the Mad and against Charles V ("the-fifth").
question.answerHtml: Revolt of the Comuneros [accept translations like Revolt of the Communities and word forms]
question.clue: A simultaneous event broke out to the south when the Germanies were formed to oppose the monarchy.

swap.text: The Flemish uprising was eventually put down by this monarch, who roasted Templar leader Jacques de Molay, feuded with Boniface VIII, and was known as "the fair."
swap.clue: He avenged his loss at the Battle of the Golden Spurs with victory at Battle of Mons-en-Pevele after which he added the Flemish cities of Lille and Douai to his holdings.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about Spain's Reconquista communities in the 11th century AD, FTPE.
question.text: The caliphate broke up into these small, independent Islamic states. When the Almoravids emerged from Africa to re-establish control in Muslim Spain, they reabsorbed these states.
question.clue: This states ruled by independent emirs, which were annexed by the Almoravids but re-emerged after the decline of the dynasty. Two of these states were ruled by the Hudids and Aftasids.

swap.leadin: They posed the last obstacle of the Reconquista. FTPE.
swap.text: After the Almohads were crushed in the Battle of Navas de Tolosa, this Moorish dynasty founded by Muhammed I al-Ghalib was the last major Muslim dynasty in Spain.
